files.reason: This lane's copy-record fragment (interface 1). Lane blindness-sidechains (the Lane-orchestrator's ruling of Sat 24 Oct 2026, under Javier's standing delegation, after pre-freeze round 1's blindness record read 45 UNEXPLAINED hits, each one inside a queued_command attachment carrying a sub-agent's hand-back, and blindness.py had never read the sub-agents' own sessions). Edits without transfer, in three files lane review-kit-port's fragment claims. review_kit/blindness.py reads every sidechain session the reviewer's session spawned (records marked isSidechain, and <session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl, matched to the Agent tool's results; a launched agent with no session file and a session file no launch names are each stated) and applies the same markers and the same absolute-path scan to each. A hand-back is read on its own, whichever record carries it (a user message, a queued command read once from its rendered form, a task notification, a foreground Agent result): a hit there is explained only when the word or path it sits in occurs in a file that was in the folder at launch and that no session wrote, and in that sub-agent's own tool traffic; an absolute path outside the folder never traces. The operator rows (lane-orchestrator, Lane Board, OrgOS, Waiting on Javier, glitch-mem, SOUL.md, north star, MEMORY.md, this repository by path, and a new row for the operator's Brain by path) are never explained, in a hand-back or in any loaded context. Writes outside the folder are listed in their own section and void nothing by themselves, and a last section states what the sub-agents' records show of the reviewer's isolation. The reviewer's launch flags are unchanged. tests/test_review_kit.py gains K15.sidechains, written red first, over one fixture reviewer session with five sub-agent session files, with 22 witnesses each red by K15.sidechains alone. review_kit/README.md's step 5 names the sidechain sessions and the sections that bind.
